The core skill script (digest_daily.py) has no compatibility issues. The benchmark worked around this by calling gather_digest() directly. Fix: replace the monkey-patch with a proper subclass or dependency injection. This is a code_fix_non_os fixability.

notes: This skill is fundamentally macOS-only. The core message sending/receiving functionality depends on: (1) AppleScript via `osascript` command to control the macOS Messages app, (2) `~/Library/Messages/chat.db` SQLite database which only exists on macOS, (3) macOS Accessibility permissions. The Python config/security management layer (trust lists, admin controls, logging) works on Linux, but this is only the administrative shell — the actual messaging capability is macOS-bound. Fixability is `not_skill_fix` because the skill's entire purpose is to interface with macOS-specific APIs. The benchmark tasks correctly validated that the authorization pipeline works cross-platform while confirming the core macOS dependency.

The bundled test suite achieves 96% pass rate (24/25) on Linux, with the single failure being a conservative detection (high vs critical).

notes: The skill is a macOS GUI automation tool with no Linux abstraction. pyobjc-framework-Vision wraps Apple's native Vision framework — the PyPI wheel only builds on macOS.
